title: Microsoft Draws $115 Billion Demand for Jumbo Debt Offering
summary: Microsoft Corp. drew blowout demand for its jumbo bond offering, as investors made room in portfolios stuffed with AI-related debt for the top-rated company’s first major issuance in almost a decade.

title: Equinix Says Data-Project Barriers Could Boost Pricing Power
summary: Equinix Inc., one of the world’s biggest data-center companies, said mounting barriers to bringing new projects online will make existing capacity more valuable and potentially strengthen its grip on the market — including pricing.

title: Toast Accused by FTC of Misleading Customers on Subscriptions
summary: The US Federal Trade Commission and a group of eight states sued Toast Inc., alleging the restaurant management and financial technology company falsely told customers they could try its products for free before enrolling them in a subscription that was difficult to cancel.

title: Marvell in Talks to Buy Nvidia-Backed Lumentum
summary: Marvell Technology is in talks to buy data center optics maker Lumentum Holdings. The deal could close next week according to sources. Nvidia backs up Lumentum which has a market value of about $83 billion. Ryan Gould reports.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Alphabet’s AI Risk Extends Beyond $1 Trillion, Filing Shows
summary: Alphabet Inc. has said demand for its cloud services is increasing at a rapid clip, pointing to growth in its backlog, or cloud contracts it hasn’t yet fulfilled. However, more than a third of that quarterly growth comes from a joint venture the company partly owns.

title: Canada, Nvidia Back Cohere in Round at Over $20 Billion Value
summary: Cohere Inc., an artificial intelligence model maker, is in the process of raising a large funding round at a $20.5 billion valuation, roughly tripling its value from a year ago.

title: Marvell Is Close to Megadeal for Laser Maker Lumentum in AI Push
summary: Marvell Technology Inc. is in advanced talks to buy data center optics maker Lumentum Holdings Inc., according to people familiar with the matter, a potential megadeal that would hand it greater control of technology critical to powering digital infrastructure.

title: Situational Awareness Pitches Investors on Fluidstack Fundraise
summary: Situational Awareness is raising money from its investors to plow into neocloud startup Fluidstack Ltd., just three months after highly levered bets on artificial intelligence firms nearly led to the hedge fund’s implosion.

title: Apple’s MacBook Pro With PROLED XDR: How the New Touch Screen Feels
summary: When buyers of Apple Inc.’s new MacBook Pro receive the company’s first touch-screen laptop, they won’t need to unlearn any habits to use it. The machine has a vivid organic light emitting diode screen — another first for the lineup — and has shaved off a noticeable amount of weight. And anyone who was worried Apple would make radical changes to its macOS operating system in the name of a more finger-friendly experience can breathe easy.

title: The Customer-Centric Agentic Enterprise
summary: The next competitive advantage from agentic AI is not cutting costs, but transforming the customer relationship. Charles Schwab’s Amy Ruegg explores how AI can help enterprises anticipate individual needs, deliver always-on service and create more personalized customer experiences at scale.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Microsoft’s AI Bet Pays Off
summary: Microsoft’s Azure growth is beating expectations, and Stifel Managing Director Brad Reback says the momentum could last with growth above 50% in the near term. He joined Bloomberg Open Interest to discuss whether Microsoft’s AI spending is paying off, why Oracle carries more risk and how public AI lab results could shed light on returns. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Cyber Race Goes Agentic
summary: Attackers and defenders are both gaining AI-powered speed and scale. Security leaders discuss how the threat landscape is changing, where new vulnerabilities are emerging and what it takes to build resilience for an increasingly autonomous enterprise.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Agentic Enterprise Starts with Your Network
summary: The future enterprise will be self-driving. As enterprises adopt agentic AI, they are on the path to greater autonomous operations. As AI agents move from insight to action, the network becomes the foundation for the agentic enterprise. This session explores how self-driving networks can accelerate autonomy, improve resilience, and help organizations keep pace with a world operating at machine speed. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The Value of Control in the Agentic Enterprise
summary: As AI moves from generating answers to taking action, the calculus is changing. Enterprise leaders discuss why control over data, infrastructure and workloads could determine who captures the value of agentic AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Nasdaq 100 Falls as AI Trade Shows New Cracks
summary: A global rally in technology shares faltered as disappointing earnings from two industry heavyweights revived doubts over whether billions of dollars in artificial-intelligence spending will deliver sufficient returns. Google parent Alphabet sank a record 13% on a sales miss, while Microsoft is looking to raise at least $25 billion from a US investment-grade bond sale. Amazon and Intel are slated to report results after Thursday's closing bell. We examine the day's top tech headlines with Gil Luria, Head of Technology Research at D.A. Davidson & Robert Schiffman, Senior Tech Credit Analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Musk’s Favorite Ticker Is Free for Taking in a SpaceX-Tesla Deal
summary: Elon Musk has an affinity for the letter X. One of Tesla Inc.’s first vehicles was the Model X. Space Exploration Technologies Corp. goes by SpaceX. Twitter was rechristened as X after Musk acquired the social media platform in 2022. He even named his son X Æ A-Xii and often refers to him as “lil X” online.

title: AI Agents Move Into the Enterprise
summary: Bloomberg Intelligence examines the accelerating shift from generative AI tools to systems that can reason, decide and act—and what that transition means for enterprise software and technology investment. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Columbia Opens Claims for $16 Million Data Breach Settlement
summary: Individuals impacted by a data breach at Columbia University can now claim part of a $16.1 million settlement reached after the university suffered a cyberattack last year.

title: Eli Lilly Raises Forecast, EBay Jumps on Results | Stock Movers
summary:
Today's biggest winners and losers in the stock market.

On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Eli Lilly (LLY) is climbing in early trading after the drugmaker boosted its revenue guidance for the full year, following better-than-expected sales in the third quarter.

- EBay (EBAY) shares jumped after the online auction company’s results and forecast were seen as underlining its strong execution and growth prospects. Wells Fargo upgraded the stock.

- Caterpillar (CAT) shares are moving after it posted quarterly earnings that beat Wall Street expectations as demand for the company's power-generation equipment continued to drive sales. The company's power and energy segment has grown into its largest business by sales, driven by technology companies' need for infrastructure to meet AI's enormous electricity demand. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: DoorDash’s $17 Billion Instacart Deal Aimed at Walmart, Amazon
summary: DoorDash Inc. agreed to buy rival Instacart in a deal that values the company at about $17 billion, the latest sign of consolidation in an increasingly competitive delivery market where Walmart Inc. and Amazon.com Inc. loom large.
